oracle.description: test_schema_check_formats.py decides correctness: 24 tests, red at the starting commit because FORMAT_CHECKERS does not exist and validate takes no assert_formats. Asserting formats by default fails 2; silently ignoring an unknown asserted format fails 2; applying format to non-strings fails 2.

purpose:
Give templates/dispatch/scripts/schema_check.py opt-in format assertion, so a schema that declares a format can have it enforced on request.

schema_check lists 'format' among its ANNOTATION_KEYWORDS. That is correct JSON Schema -- format is an annotation unless a validator opts into asserting it -- but it means manifest.schema.json's "format": "uuid" on authority_repo_uuid is enforced nowhere, and the checker will certify a non-UUID there while claiming to enforce every construct it accepts.

Do NOT start asserting formats by default. validate() is on the live dispatch path and every manifest in /projects/dev is checked with it, so assertion must be something a caller asks for, never something that arrives with an upgrade. 'format' must also REMAIN in ANNOTATION_KEYWORDS, so a schema naming a format nobody asserts does not become unauditable.

Add two things:
  FORMAT_CHECKERS -- a dict from format name to a predicate over a string. It must contain 'uuid'. A caller reads it to discover what can be asserted.
  validate(instance, schema, path='$', assert_formats=()) -- assert_formats names the formats to enforce for this call, and accepts any iterable. Empty (the default) must behave exactly as today.

Two rules keep this honest rather than decorative:
  * a name in assert_formats with no entry in FORMAT_CHECKERS raises UnsupportedKeyword -- even when the schema does not mention that format. Silently ignoring it is exactly the defect being repaired: certifying what was never checked.
  * format constrains STRINGS ONLY. A number or a null under a format schema is not a violation; the 'type' keyword is what constrains type.

Assertion must reach nested properties and array items, not only the top level, so thread the asserted set through the recursive core.

The uuid checker accepts the canonical hyphenated form, case-insensitively, and rejects the URN (urn:uuid:...) and braced ({...}) spellings, a wrong length, a non-hex character, and the unhyphenated form. Accepting three spellings for one identifier is how two records of the same thing stop comparing equal.

Error text must name the path and the format.
required_outcomes: FORMAT_CHECKERS exists, maps names to callables, and contains 'uuid'
validate with no assert_formats behaves exactly as before, including on the real manifest schema
a name in assert_formats with no checker raises UnsupportedKeyword, schema or no schema
assertion reaches nested properties and array items
the uuid checker accepts the canonical form case-insensitively and rejects urn, braced, wrong length, non-hex and unhyphenated
the error text names the path and the format

acceptance_properties.requirement: assertion is opt-in and the live path does not move
acceptance_properties.fails_when: a bad value fails validation when no format was asserted, or the real manifest schema stops auditing clean

acceptance_properties.requirement: the checker never certifies what it cannot check
acceptance_properties.fails_when: an assert_formats name with no registered checker is ignored instead of raising
a number or null under a format schema is reported as a violation
the urn, braced or unhyphenated uuid spellings are accepted

non_goals: changing manifest.schema.json, which is protected at the manifest level
turning assertion on for any existing caller -- that is a separate coordinator decision
adding checkers for formats beyond uuid
